facts.text: Redfield was founded in 1878, when settlers first arrived and a post office opened as Stennett Junction before the town adopted its current name in 1881.
The town grew into a railroad hub, sitting at the crossroads of the Chicago and North Western Railway and the Milwaukee Road Railroad.
Redfield became Spink County’s seat in 1886 after a six‑year legal battle among neighboring towns.
Redfield College opened in 1887 and served the community until 1932, leaving a legacy of early higher‑education in the region.
In 1902 the Northern Hospital for the Insane opened just north of town, a facility that still operates today as the South Dakota Developmental Center.
Three U.S. Presidents—William McKinley, William Howard Taft, and Franklin D. Roosevelt—visited Redfield during their travels in the early 20th century.
